[AudioSilo](https://audiosilo.app) is a self-hosted audiobook server. Point it at your audiobook folders and listen from the built-in web player or the AudioSilo apps for iOS and Android, with listening progress synced across devices.

[![audiosilo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/linuxserver/docker-templates/master/linuxserver.io/img/audiosilo-logo.png)](https://audiosilo.app)

## Supported Architectures

We utilise the docker manifest for multi-platform awareness. More information is available from docker [here](https://distribution.github.io/distribution/spec/manifest-v2-2/#manifest-list) and our announcement [here](https://blog.linuxserver.io/2019/02/21/the-lsio-pipeline-project/).

Simply pulling `ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/audiosilo:latest` should retrieve the correct image for your arch, but you can also pull specific arch images via tags.

The architectures supported by this image are:

| Architecture | Available | Tag |
| :----: | :----: | ---- |
| x86-64 | ✅ | amd64-\<version tag\> |
| arm64 | ✅ | arm64v8-\<version tag\> |

## Application Setup

On first start AudioSilo creates an admin account and prints its password, plus an auth code for pairing devices, to the container log **once**, so check the log straight away (`docker logs audiosilo`).

The server listens on HTTPS with a self-signed certificate by default. Open `https://<your-ip>:8080/admin`, accept the certificate warning, sign in as `admin`, and add `/audiobooks` as a library. The web player is at `/web`. To connect a phone, enter the auth code on the page at `/`; it then shows the QR code the AudioSilo app scans.

Settings live in the admin console under **Server > Settings**, saved to `/config/config.yaml`. To run behind a reverse proxy such as SWAG, either proxy to the HTTPS port as is, or set **HTTPS mode** to **Off** (then restart the container) and let the proxy terminate TLS. Either way, set **Public address** to the proxied URL so invite links and pairing QR codes point there, and add the proxy's address to **Trusted proxies** so rate limiting sees your visitors' real addresses.

Any `AUDIOSILO_*` environment variable overrides its setting and shows as locked in the admin console. See the [configuration reference](https://docs.audiosilo.app/developers/server/configuration#environment-variables) for the full list.

### Strict reverse proxies

This image uses a self-signed certificate by default. This naturally means the scheme is `https`.
If you are using a reverse proxy which validates certificates, you need to [disable this check for the container](https://linuxserver-playground.github.io/site/docs/faq#strict-proxy).

## Read-Only Operation

This image can be run with a read-only container filesystem. For details please [read the docs](https://linuxserver-playground.github.io/site/docs/misc/read-only/).

## Non-Root Operation

This image can be run with a non-root user. For details please [read the docs](https://linuxserver-playground.github.io/site/docs/misc/non-root/).

## Usage

To help you get started creating a container from this image you can either use docker-compose or the docker cli.

!!! info

    Unless a parameter is flagged as 'optional', it is *mandatory* and a value must be provided.

### docker-compose (recommended, [click here for more info](https://linuxserver-playground.github.io/site/docs/general/docker-compose))

```yaml
---
services:
  audiosilo:
    image: ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/audiosilo:latest
    container_name: audiosilo
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=Etc/UTC
    volumes:
      - /path/to/audiosilo/config:/config
      - /path/to/audiobooks:/audiobooks:ro
    ports:
      - 8080:8080
    restart: unless-stopped
```

### docker cli ([click here for more info](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/cli/))

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name=audiosilo \
  -e PUID=1000 \
  -e PGID=1000 \
  -e TZ=Etc/UTC \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  -v /path/to/audiosilo/config:/config \
  -v /path/to/audiobooks:/audiobooks:ro \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/audiosilo:latest
```

## Parameters

Containers are configured using parameters passed at runtime (such as those above). These parameters are separated by a colon and indicate `<external>:<internal>` respectively. For example, `-p 8080:80` would expose port `80` from inside the container to be accessible from the host's IP on port `8080` outside the container.

### Ports (`-p`)

| Parameter | Function |
| :----: | --- |
| `8080:8080` | Web player, admin console and the API the apps connect to. |

### Environment Variables (`-e`)

| Env | Function |
| :----: | --- |
| `PUID=1000` | for UserID - see below for explanation |
| `PGID=1000` | for GroupID - see below for explanation |
| `TZ=Etc/UTC` | specify a timezone to use, see this [list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones#List). |

### Volume Mappings (`-v`)

| Volume | Function |
| :----: | --- |
| `/config` | Persistent config files, database, backups and TLS certificates. |
| `/audiobooks:ro` | Audiobooks location, read-only (the server never writes to your books). Add it as a library in the admin console. |

#### Miscellaneous Options

| Parameter | Function |
| :-----:   | --- |
| `--read-only=true` | Run container with a read-only filesystem. Please [read the docs](https://linuxserver-playground.github.io/site/docs/misc/read-only/). |
| `--user=1000:1000` | Run container with a non-root user. Please [read the docs](https://linuxserver-playground.github.io/site/docs/misc/non-root/). |

## Environment variables from files (Docker secrets)

You can set any environment variable from a file by using a special prepend `FILE__`.

As an example:

```bash
-e FILE__MYVAR=/run/secrets/mysecretvariable
```

Will set the environment variable `MYVAR` based on the contents of the `/run/secrets/mysecretvariable` file.

## Umask for running applications

For all of our images we provide the ability to override the default umask settings for services started within the containers using the optional `-e UMASK=022` setting.
Keep in mind umask is not chmod it subtracts from permissions based on it's value it does not add. Please read up [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umask) before asking for support.

## User / Group Identifiers

When using volumes (`-v` flags), permissions issues can arise between the host OS and the container, we avoid this issue by allowing you to specify the user `PUID` and group `PGID`.

Ensure any volume directories on the host are owned by the same user you specify and any permissions issues will vanish like magic.

In this instance `PUID=1000` and `PGID=1000`, to find yours use `id your_user` as below:

```bash
id your_user
```

Example output:

```text
uid=1000(your_user) gid=1000(your_user) groups=1000(your_user)
```

## Updating Info

Most of our images are static, versioned, and require an image update and container recreation to update the app inside. With some exceptions (noted in the relevant readme.md), we do not recommend or support updating apps inside the container. Please consult the [Application Setup](#application-setup) section above to see if it is recommended for the image.

Below are the instructions for updating containers:

### Via Docker Compose

* Update images:
    * All images:

        ```bash
        docker-compose pull
        ```

    * Single image:

        ```bash
        docker-compose pull audiosilo
        ```

* Update containers:
    * All containers:

        ```bash
        docker-compose up -d
        ```

    * Single container:

        ```bash
        docker-compose up -d audiosilo
        ```

* You can also remove the old dangling images:

    ```bash
    docker image prune
    ```

### Via Docker Run

* Update the image:

    ```bash
    docker pull ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/audiosilo:latest
    ```

* Stop the running container:

    ```bash
    docker stop audiosilo
    ```

* Delete the container:

    ```bash
    docker rm audiosilo
    ```

* Recreate a new container with the same docker run parameters as instructed above (if mapped correctly to a host folder, your `/config` folder and settings will be preserved)
* You can also remove the old dangling images:

    ```bash
    docker image prune
    ```

### Image Update Notifications - Diun (Docker Image Update Notifier)

!!! tip

    We recommend [Diun](https://crazymax.dev/diun/) for update notifications. Other tools that automatically update containers unattended are not recommended or supported.

## Building locally

If you want to make local modifications to these images for development purposes or just to customize the logic:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/linuxserver-playground/docker-audiosilo.git
cd docker-audiosilo
docker build \
  --no-cache \
  --pull \
  -t ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/audiosilo:latest .
```

The ARM variants can be built on x86_64 hardware and vice versa using `ghcr.io/linuxserver/qemu-static`

```bash
docker run --rm --privileged ghcr.io/linuxserver/qemu-static --reset
```

Once registered you can define the dockerfile to use with `-f Dockerfile.aarch64`.

Every push builds and tests the image with the shared workflow in [`linuxserver-playground/workflows`](https://github.com/linuxserver-playground/workflows); every build's tests, screenshots and package changes are on [the image's builds](https://linuxserver-playground.github.io/site/images/audiosilo/#builds) on the website.
